1.summary: Paul thanks God for the Thessalonians' growing faith and love amid persecution, assures them that God is just and will repay their persecutors when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven, and prays that God will make them worthy of their calling.
1.lookfor: Notice how Paul frames their suffering, and the contrast between the fate of persecutors and believers.

insights.title: Growing exceedingly
insights.body: Their faith grows exceedingly and their love abounds (1:3). Paul's prayers from the first letter were answered.

insights.title: Evidence of God's justice
insights.body: Their endurance is a sign of God's righteous judgment, that they will be counted worthy of the kingdom for which they suffer (1:5). Suffering isn't proof of God's absence.

insights.title: Rest with us
insights.body: God will repay affliction to those who afflict you, and give rest to you who are afflicted, along with us (1:6-7). Justice will come, and it is God's to give, not theirs to take.

insights.title: In flaming fire
insights.body: The Lord Jesus will be revealed from heaven with his mighty angels in flaming fire (1:7-8). Old Testament pictures of the Lord coming in fire are applied to Jesus.

insights.title: Away from the presence
insights.body: Those who reject the gospel will suffer eternal destruction, away from the presence of the Lord (1:9). At its core, judgment is separation from the one who is the source of all good.

insights.title: Glorified in his saints
insights.body: Christ comes to be glorified in his saints and admired among all who believe (1:10). His people will reflect his glory.

insights.title: Leaving justice to God
insights.body: Paul assures persecuted believers that God will set things right. What wrong done to you do you need to leave in God's hands?

2.summary: Paul corrects the claim that the day of the Lord has already come: first must come the rebellion and the man of lawlessness, who is now restrained and whom the Lord Jesus will destroy at his coming; Paul thanks God for choosing them and urges them to hold fast to his teaching.
2.lookfor: Notice what must happen before the day of the Lord, and the comfort Paul gives at the end.

names.name: Satan
names.gloss: The power behind the man of lawlessness.

insights.title: A forged letter?
insights.body: Paul warns them not to be shaken by a spirit, word or letter as if from us claiming the day of the Lord has come (2:2). Someone may have circulated a letter in Paul's name, which is why he signs this one himself.

insights.title: Not yet
insights.body: That day won't come unless the rebellion comes first and the man of lawlessness is revealed (2:3). The Thessalonians hadn't missed it.

insights.title: The man of lawlessness
insights.body: He exalts himself above every god and sits in God's temple, proclaiming himself God (2:4). The picture draws on Daniel's arrogant king and recalls the emperor Caligula's attempt to set up his statue in the Jerusalem temple about ten years earlier.

insights.title: The restrainer
insights.body: Something, and someone, is restraining him until the right time (2:6-7). Paul had told them what it was; we don't know. Suggestions include the Roman state, the preaching of the gospel and God's own Spirit. Readers have debated it for centuries.

insights.title: The breath of his mouth
insights.body: The Lord Jesus will destroy him with the breath of his mouth (2:8), from Isaiah's prophecy of the shoot from Jesse who slays the wicked with his breath.

insights.title: Chosen and called
insights.body: God chose you from the beginning for salvation, through sanctification by the Spirit and belief of the truth, and called you through the gospel (2:13-14). Whatever comes, they belong to him.

insights.title: Not shaken
insights.body: Paul doesn't want them alarmed by every rumor about the end. What fears about the future unsettle you, and what truth steadies you?

3.summary: Paul asks for prayer, expresses confidence in the Lord's faithfulness, and commands believers to keep away from those living in idleness, reminding them that he worked to support himself and that whoever won't work shouldn't eat; he closes with his own signature.
3.lookfor: Notice how Paul handles the idle, firm but treating them as brothers.

insights.title: That the word may run
insights.body: Pray that the word of the Lord may run swiftly and be glorified (3:1). Paul pictures the message as a runner.

insights.title: The Lord is faithful
insights.body: Not everyone has faith, but the Lord is faithful; he will establish you and guard you from the evil one (3:2-3). Our security rests on his faithfulness.

insights.title: The idle
insights.body: Some were living in idleness, busybodies not busy at work (3:11). Perhaps they thought Jesus' return made work pointless, or wealthy believers were supporting them as clients.

insights.title: No work, no food
insights.body: If anyone won't work, neither let him eat (3:10). Note the word won't: this is about refusing to work, not inability to find work.

insights.title: An example
insights.body: Paul had the right to support but worked night and day to give himself as an example, typos, a model to copy (3:9).

insights.title: Not an enemy
insights.body: Keep away from one who disobeys, so he may be ashamed, yet don't count him as an enemy, but admonish him as a brother (3:14-15). Church discipline aims to restore.

insights.title: Don't tire of doing good
insights.body: Paul says, don't be weary in doing well (3:13). Where is your energy for doing good running low?

intro.who: Paul, Silvanus and Timothy (1:1), again to the Thessalonians. Paul signs it himself (3:17). Some scholars think a later follower wrote it; many accept it as Paul's.
intro.when: About AD 51, from Corinth, probably a few months after 1 Thessalonians.
intro.why: Persecution had grown, and some were alarmed by a claim, perhaps in a forged letter, that the day of the Lord had already come; others had stopped working. Paul encourages them that God will put things right, explains what must happen first, and tells the idle to get back to work.

outline.title: The day of the Lord has not yet come
